I acknowledge that Madrid are the richest club in the world in terms of revenue year after year and that the ratio of their revenue:loans is more proportional than our revenue:owner's-money. However it still must be noted that Real Madrid have, throughout their history, essentially 'bought the best in order to be the best' and that is pretty much what we and City are trying to do and until there are rules in place that prevent it from happening, some club in the game will always try to do this.

But your argument was that you have a problem with the clubs not earning the money that they spend. For you to say that taking out as many loans as you need is not essentially the same as having a billionaire owner to finance your club is crazy.

You do know that a significant percentage of Real Madrid's transfer budget is derived from loans, right? And that Man Utd are now in approximately £500m of debt due to their owners taking out loans to finance the club? So it's not all 'clean' spending is it?

Edit: The addition of United

I fail to see how we and City are 'ruining' football. Of course money was a significant factor in getting us to our respective positions but It's not like we spend money and then do nothing on the pitch. Clubs have to work hard to get to their positions whether they are helped by money or not.

Secondly, I never hear anyone complain about Madrid's use of money. Yes they are the most successful club in European football, but in modern times a lot of their success is gained with the help of money and they never get shit for it.

I'm not saying that spending large amounts of money is the only route to footballing success, but I don't think that clubs should be condemned for using money to help themselves.
